schema_lineage.purpose: Extended maturity self-assessment framework for secure-by-design AI technology and service capabilities — incorporating full AIUC-1 compliance requirements for AI agent security, safety, reliability, accountability, societal risk, and data privacy. Targeting Chief Product Officers (CPOs), product security leaders, and compliance teams responsible for embedding security, trust, and accountability into AI-powered products and services.
schema_lineage.changelog: v2.0 extends v1.0 by mapping all 44 AIUC-1 requirements across 6 AIUC-1 categories (Data & Privacy, Security, Safety, Reliability, Accountability, Society) into the existing 5-pillar structure and adding 2 new pillars (SAF — AI Output Safety, REL — AI Reliability & Tool Safety). Sub-pillar count increased from 25 to 40. Every AIUC-1 requirement is traceable to at least one sub-pillar via the aiuc1_mapping field.

secure_by_design_ai_controls_v2.0.intent: Assess organizational maturity across 40 control dimensions spanning infrastructure, identity, network/data, DevSecOps/MLSecOps, AI TRiSM, output safety, and reliability. Each sub-pillar is scored 1–5 on a maturity scale. The framework extends v1.0 with AIUC-1 compliance coverage — adding explicit controls for AI output safety (harmful outputs, out-of-scope, output vulnerabilities), data consent and IP protection, AI disclosure mechanisms, third-party testing mandates, hallucination prevention, tool call safety, societal risk guardrails, and accountability structures. Every AIUC-1 requirement (A001–F002) maps to one or more sub-pillars.

metadata.framework_alignment: NIST AI RMF 1.0 + AI 600-1 (GenAI Profile) + AI RMF Playbook + COSAiS (SP 800-53 Overlays for AI) + AIUC-1 (AI Agent Security, Safety & Reliability Standard) + MITRE ATLAS + ISO 42001 + EU AI Act + OWASP Top 10 for LLM/GenAI
metadata.target_audience: Chief Product Officers (CPOs), VP Product Security, AI/ML Engineering Leads, GRC Teams, Compliance Officers

scoring_logic.1: Not Started — No controls, processes, or awareness in this area. The organization has not begun addressing this dimension.
scoring_logic.2: Ad Hoc / Initial — Informal, reactive, or person-dependent practices exist. No documented policy or repeatable process. Controls may be applied inconsistently.
scoring_logic.3: Defined / Repeatable — Documented policies and procedures exist. Controls are applied consistently across most AI workloads but measurement is limited. Some tooling in place.
scoring_logic.4: Managed / Measured — Controls are enforced via automation or tooling, with defined metrics and KPIs. Evidence is collected systematically. Regular reviews occur. Exceptions are tracked.
scoring_logic.5: Optimized / Adaptive — Continuous improvement driven by metrics, threat intelligence, and lessons learned. Controls self-adapt or are proactively tuned. Full auditability, cross-framework mapping, and executive reporting in place.

evidence_expectations.description: Each maturity level should be supported by evidence artifacts appropriate to the level.

by_level.2: Informal notes, tribal knowledge, ad hoc procedures
by_level.3: Documented policies, architecture diagrams, runbooks, tool configurations
by_level.4: Automated dashboards, audit logs, KPI reports, test results, control validation records
by_level.5: Continuous assurance reports, executive dashboards, cross-framework crosswalks, improvement trend data, third-party attestations

coverage_grade.description: Letter grade based on percentage of sub-pillars scoring ≥3 (Defined or above)

aiuc1_compliance_summary.description: AIUC-1 compliance tracking — maps each AIUC-1 requirement to the sub-pillar(s) that address it.

INF.name: Infrastructure for AI
INF.focus: Hardened, isolated, and cryptographically protected compute and runtime environments for AI training, fine-tuning, and inference — with supply-chain assurance, vendor due diligence, and deployment environment security for all AI components.
nist_references: AI RMF Playbook — Secure & Resilient, Operation & Monitoring
maturity_signals: Dedicated VNETs/VPCs with private endpoints for AI workloads
Auditable GPU/TPU provisioning with RBAC
AES-256 or equivalent encryption at rest for models, weights, datasets
TLS 1.3+ encryption in transit for all model-serving and pipeline traffic
SBOM and provenance tracking for AI frameworks, pretrained models, and agents
Documented cloud vs. on-premises processing criteria for AI workloads
Vendor due diligence covering data handling, PII controls, and compliance

IAM.name: Identity, Access & Disclosure for AI
IAM.focus: Fine-grained identity, authentication, and authorization controls for AI workspaces, APIs, agents, and human-in-the-loop approval workflows — plus AI disclosure mechanisms and controls against technical over-disclosure.
maturity_signals: RBAC/ABAC enforced across AI workspaces, model registries, and datasets
Managed identities and scoped tokens for all AI API endpoints
HITL approval gates for high-risk AI actions
Policy-aware prompt/response guardrails with role-based redaction
Non-human identity lifecycle management for AI agents
AI disclosure mechanisms informing users of AI interaction
Controls preventing over-disclosure of system architecture details

B003.requirement: Manage public release of technical details

B007.requirement: Enforce user access privileges to AI systems

NDS.name: Network, Data Security & Privacy for AI
NDS.focus: Network isolation, boundary defenses, secure data pipelines, inference monitoring, data sovereignty, consent-based data policies, cross-customer isolation, and intellectual property safeguards purpose-built for AI workloads.
nist_references: AI RMF Playbook — Secure Operations, Data & Drift
COSAiS — component-level controls for training/test data
maturity_signals: Air-gapped or broker-mediated training networks
WAF + rate limiting + prompt-injection filtering at inference endpoints
Data provenance, integrity hashing, and poisoning/drift monitoring
Inference request/response logging with exfiltration detection
Data residency and sovereignty enforcement for AI datasets
Published AI input/output data policies with customer consent mechanisms
Multi-tenant data isolation preventing cross-customer exposure
IP and copyright safeguards in AI output generation

DSO.name: DevSecOps for AI (MLSecOps)
DSO.focus: Secure ML CI/CD, model/dataset lineage and versioning, pre-release testing and validation (TEVV), risk-gated deployment, production auditability through lineage graphs, and mandated independent third-party testing programs.
nist_references: AI RMF Playbook — TEVV, Governance & Documentation
maturity_signals: Dependency scanning and model signing in ML CI/CD pipelines
Immutable model/dataset versioning with rollback capability
Red-team, adversarial, bias, and safety testing before every release
Staged rollout with kill-switch and HITL escalation
Graph-based audit trail linking code → data → model → decision → outcome
Quarterly third-party testing across safety, security, and reliability risk categories

E007.requirement: Document system change approvals (merged with E004)
E007.note: Merged with E004 in Q1 2026 update

TRM.name: AI TRiSM (Trust, Risk & Security Management)
TRM.focus: Model governance, use-case risk assessment, trustworthiness controls, AI-specific incident response with failure plans, lineage and accountability graph, quality management systems, enterprise framework crosswalks, and societal risk prevention.
nist_references: AI RMF Playbook — Governance & Oversight, Explainability, Fairness & Bias, Privacy
maturity_signals: Formal model approval, ownership, lifecycle, and retirement processes with acceptable use policies
Per-use-case AI risk assessments with stakeholder impact mapping
Bias, explainability, privacy, and robustness controls with metrics and transparency reports
AI-specific incident response runbooks and documented failure plans for security breaches, harmful outputs, and hallucinations
Accountability graph connecting model decisions to governance artifacts and outcomes
Maintained crosswalk to NIST CSF, ISO 42001, EU AI Act, AIUC-1
Quality management system for AI processes proportionate to organization size
Societal risk guardrails preventing AI-enabled cyber misuse and CBRN exploitation

E001.requirement: AI failure plan for security breaches

E002.requirement: AI failure plan for harmful outputs

E014.note: Merged with E017 in Q1 2026 update

SAF.name: AI Output Safety
SAF.focus: Systematic prevention, detection, and escalation of harmful, out-of-scope, and vulnerable AI outputs — covering risk taxonomy definition, output safety controls, scope boundary enforcement, monitoring with human escalation, and output limitation mechanisms. Primary alignment with AIUC-1 Category C (Safety) and B009.
nist_references: AI RMF Playbook — Trustworthy Characteristics (Safety, Fairness, Explainability)
OWASP Top 10 for LLM — Output Handling
maturity_signals: Published AI risk taxonomy covering harmful, out-of-scope, and hallucinated output categories with severity ratings
Technical controls preventing harmful outputs (distressed, angry, offensive, biased, deceptive)
Scope boundary enforcement preventing out-of-scope and policy-violating outputs
Automated flagging of high-risk outputs for human review with real-time intervention
Output limitation and obfuscation preventing information leakage and adversarial exploitation

REL.name: AI Reliability & Tool Safety
REL.focus: Prevention and detection of hallucinated outputs and unsafe tool calls — ensuring AI systems produce factually grounded responses and that agentic tool interactions remain within authorized scope. Primary alignment with AIUC-1 Category D (Reliability).
nist_references: OWASP Top 10 for LLM — Hallucinations, Tool/Plugin Risks
maturity_signals: Technical controls preventing hallucinated outputs (grounding, RAG, verification chains)
Safeguards restricting AI tool calls to authorized actions, scopes, and information
Independent third-party testing for hallucination rates and tool call safety

INF-01.name: Hardened AI Runtime Isolation
INF-01.expanded_definition: Dedicated, hardened compute environments for AI training, fine-tuning, and inference — using VNETs, VPCs, private endpoints, and container/VM isolation to minimize blast radius and lateral movement risk. Includes deployment environment protection with encryption, access controls, and authorization.
INF-01.ai_rmf_mapping: Govern / Manage / Measure — governance of deployment patterns, managed risk treatments, continuous evaluation of infrastructure risk.
maturity_criteria: Dedicated VNETs/VPCs for AI workloads separate from general compute
Private endpoints for model registries, training clusters, and inference APIs
Container and VM hardening (CIS benchmarks, minimal images, runtime security)
Network micro-segmentation between training, staging, and production AI environments
Automated drift detection for infrastructure configuration
Documented criteria for cloud vs. on-premises AI processing based on data sensitivity, regulatory requirements, and security controls (AIUC-1 E005)
Encryption, access controls, and authorization hardening for model deployment environments (AIUC-1 B008)

INF-02.name: Compute Access Governance
INF-02.expanded_definition: Controlled, auditable access to high-value AI compute resources (GPU/TPU clusters) with least-privilege provisioning, cost controls, and usage accountability.
INF-02.ai_rmf_mapping: Govern / Manage / Measure — role clarity and least privilege with effectiveness checks.
maturity_criteria: RBAC for GPU/TPU cluster provisioning and scheduling
Auditable request/approval workflow for compute allocation
Cost and usage monitoring with anomaly alerting
Time-bounded and project-scoped compute reservations
Automated deprovisioning of idle or expired compute resources

INF-03.name: Encryption at Rest
INF-03.expanded_definition: Cryptographic protection of all AI artifacts at rest — including trained models, model weights, training datasets, evaluation datasets, configuration files, and intermediate artifacts — using enterprise key management.
INF-03.ai_rmf_mapping: Manage / Measure — secure & resilient outcomes and verification.
maturity_criteria: AES-256 (or equivalent) encryption for all stored models and weights
Encryption of training and evaluation datasets in object storage and databases
Hardware Security Module (HSM) or cloud KMS for key management
Key rotation policies enforced automatically on a defined schedule
Encryption coverage audit and gap reporting

INF-04.name: Encryption in Transit
INF-04.expanded_definition: Cryptographic protection of all AI-related data in motion — including model-serving API traffic, training data pipeline transfers, model distribution, and inter-service communication — using modern transport security.
INF-04.ai_rmf_mapping: Manage / Measure — secure & resilient outcomes and verification.
maturity_criteria: TLS 1.3+ enforced on all model-serving and inference API endpoints
Encrypted data pipelines for training data ingestion and transfer
mTLS (mutual TLS) between AI microservices and internal endpoints
Certificate lifecycle management with automated renewal
Network traffic inspection confirming no plaintext AI data in transit

INF-05.name: AI Supply Chain & Vendor Assurance
INF-05.expanded_definition: Verification, provenance tracking, and risk assessment for all AI supply-chain components — including ML frameworks, pretrained models, third-party agents, training data sources, and open-source dependencies. Extended with AIUC-1 vendor due diligence processes for foundation model providers.
INF-05.ai_rmf_mapping: Map / Govern / Manage — dependency mapping, policy setting, risk treatment.
maturity_criteria: SBOM (Software Bill of Materials) for all AI pipeline components
Provenance verification for pretrained models and foundation models
Vulnerability scanning of ML frameworks and dependencies
Vendor/source risk assessment for third-party AI components
Automated alerting on supply-chain compromise indicators
AI vendor due diligence process for foundation and upstream model providers covering data handling, PII controls, security, and compliance (AIUC-1 E006)
Open-source AI component risk assessment with license and provenance review

IAM-01.name: Fine-Grained AI Workspace IAM
IAM-01.expanded_definition: Role-based (RBAC) and attribute-based (ABAC) access controls applied to AI workspaces, model registries, datasets, feature stores, and inference endpoints — enforcing least privilege across the AI lifecycle. Includes enforcement of user access controls and admin privileges per organizational policy.
IAM-01.ai_rmf_mapping: Govern / Manage — role definitions, least privilege, operational enforcement.

B007.requirement: Enforce user access privileges to AI systems

maturity_criteria: RBAC policies defined for AI platform roles (data scientist, ML engineer, reviewer, admin)
ABAC policies incorporating project, data classification, and environment attributes
Separation of duties between model development, approval, and deployment
Access reviews and recertification on a defined cadence
Integration with enterprise IdP (SSO, MFA) for all AI platform access
User access controls and admin privileges established and maintained in line with organizational AI policy (AIUC-1 B007)

IAM-02.name: AI API Authorization & HITL Approvals
IAM-02.expanded_definition: Strong authentication and authorization for AI APIs using managed identities, scoped tokens, and API keys — combined with human-in-the-loop (HITL) approval gates for high-risk or high-impact AI actions. Includes monitoring of third-party access to AI systems.
IAM-02.ai_rmf_mapping: Manage / Measure — operational controls plus control-efficacy review.
maturity_criteria: Managed identities or service principals for all AI API endpoints
Scoped API keys with expiration and usage limits per consumer
HITL approval workflows for model deployments, retraining triggers, and data access
Token-based authentication with short-lived access tokens (OAuth 2.0 / OIDC)
Audit logging of all API authorization decisions including denials
Systems to monitor and audit third-party access to AI systems and APIs (AIUC-1 E009)

IAM-03.name: Prompt & Response Guardrails by Role
IAM-03.expanded_definition: Policy-aware input/output controls that filter, redact, or block AI interactions based on the requester's role, data classification of the context, and organizational content policies. Extended with real-time input filtering using automated moderation tools.
IAM-03.ai_rmf_mapping: Manage / Measure — TEVV and monitoring for harmful outputs.
maturity_criteria: Role-based prompt policies (e.g., restricting PII queries for non-privileged users)
Automated response redaction based on data classification
Content safety filters for harmful, biased, or policy-violating outputs
Jailbreak and prompt-injection detection with alert/block actions
Policy versioning and audit trail for guardrail rule changes
Real-time input filtering using automated moderation tools for prompt injection, jailbreak, and adversarial input protection (AIUC-1 B005)

IAM-04.name: AI Agent Identity, Delegation & Scope
IAM-04.expanded_definition: Identity management for non-human AI agents — including unique agent identities, scoped delegation of authority, action boundaries, revocable trust chains for agentic AI workflows, and data collection limitations ensuring agents access only task-relevant information.
IAM-04.ai_rmf_mapping: Govern / Manage — role definitions and operational enforcement for autonomous agents.
maturity_criteria: Unique, auditable identities assigned to each AI agent instance
Scoped delegation policies defining what actions agents may perform
Action boundary enforcement (resource limits, allowed APIs, data scopes)
Revocable trust chains with real-time suspension capability
Agent activity logging with attribution to originating user or workflow
Safeguards preventing AI agents from performing actions beyond intended scope and authorized privileges (AIUC-1 B006)
Data collection limitations ensuring AI agent access is restricted to task-relevant information based on user roles and context (AIUC-1 A003)

IAM-05.name: AI Disclosure & Technical Exposure Controls
IAM-05.expanded_definition: Controls ensuring users are informed when they interact with AI systems rather than humans, and preventing over-disclosure of technical implementation details that could enable adversarial targeting. Covers AI labeling, transparency notifications, and information security for system architecture details.
IAM-05.ai_rmf_mapping: Govern / Manage — transparency obligations and information security.

B003.requirement: Manage public release of technical details

maturity_criteria: Clear disclosure mechanisms informing users when they interact with AI systems rather than humans (AIUC-1 E016)
AI interaction labeling applied consistently across all customer-facing AI touchpoints
Controls preventing over-disclosure of AI system architecture, model details, and organizational information that could enable adversarial targeting (AIUC-1 B003)
Policy governing public release of AI technical details (research papers, blog posts, open-source) with security review
Disclosure and labeling audit trail demonstrating consistent application

NDS-01.name: Segregated Training Networks
NDS-01.expanded_definition: Network isolation for AI training environments — no direct internet egress, brokered or air-gapped data transfer, and dedicated network segments to prevent data leakage and supply-chain injection during training.
NDS-01.ai_rmf_mapping: Govern / Manage — policy-driven isolation and operational guardrails.
maturity_criteria: Training environments on isolated network segments with no direct internet access
Brokered data transfer via approved gateways with integrity checks
Egress filtering and DLP controls on training network boundaries
Separate DNS and proxy configurations for training vs. production
Network flow logging and anomaly detection for training segments

NDS-02.name: Model Boundary Defenses
NDS-02.expanded_definition: Perimeter and application-layer defenses purpose-built for AI inference endpoints — including web application firewalls, rate limiting, abuse detection, prompt-injection/jailbreak filtering, endpoint scraping prevention, and adversarial input detection.
NDS-02.ai_rmf_mapping: Manage / Measure — resilience and adversarial testing outcomes.
maturity_criteria: WAF rules tuned for LLM endpoint attack patterns
Rate limiting and throttling per consumer, API key, and IP
Prompt-injection and jailbreak detection with real-time blocking
Model extraction and model-stealing defense mechanisms
Adversarial input detection (e.g., perturbation attacks on classification models)
Safeguards preventing probing or scraping of external AI endpoints including query quotas and zero-trust policies (AIUC-1 B004)
Monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to adversarial inputs and prompt injection attempts in real time (AIUC-1 B002)

NDS-03.name: Secure Data Pipelines
NDS-03.expanded_definition: End-to-end security for AI data pipelines — covering data provenance, integrity verification, labeling governance, and monitoring for data poisoning and distribution drift.
NDS-03.ai_rmf_mapping: Map / Measure / Manage — context, continuous measurement, risk response.
maturity_criteria: Data provenance tracking from source to training/evaluation usage
Cryptographic integrity checks (hashing) on datasets at each pipeline stage
Data labeling governance with quality assurance and reviewer audit trails
Automated monitoring for data poisoning, contamination, and anomalous inputs
Distribution drift detection with alerting and retraining triggers

NDS-04.name: Inference Logging, PII Protection & Exfiltration Monitoring
NDS-04.expanded_definition: Comprehensive logging of AI inference requests and responses — with monitoring for data exfiltration attempts, anomalous usage patterns, unauthorized knowledge extraction, and specific safeguards against PII leakage through AI outputs and logs.
NDS-04.ai_rmf_mapping: Measure / Manage — ongoing risk monitoring and response.
maturity_criteria: Structured logging of all inference requests and responses (or representative samples)
Anomaly detection on query patterns (volume spikes, systematic probing, enumeration)
Data exfiltration monitoring for PII, trade secrets, or training data leakage in outputs
Integration with SIEM/SOAR for automated alert and response workflows
Retention policies aligned with compliance and forensic requirements
Safeguards preventing personal data (PII) leakage through AI outputs and logs with automated detection and redaction (AIUC-1 A006)
Comprehensive logging of AI system processes, actions, and model outputs to support incident investigation, auditing, and explanation of AI behavior (AIUC-1 E015)

NDS-05.name: Data Sovereignty, Privacy & Regulatory Controls
NDS-05.expanded_definition: Controls ensuring AI training data, model artifacts, and inference data comply with data residency, sovereignty, and privacy regulations — including GDPR, sector-specific mandates, cross-border transfer restrictions, and documented processing locations.
NDS-05.ai_rmf_mapping: Govern / Manage — policy-driven data governance and compliance.
maturity_criteria: Data residency enforcement for AI datasets and model storage by jurisdiction
Cross-border data transfer controls with legal basis documentation
Privacy impact assessments (PIAs) for AI workloads processing personal data
Data minimization and purpose limitation enforced in training data selection
Right-to-erasure and data subject request workflows for AI training data
Documented AI data processing locations with maintained records of where data is stored and processed (AIUC-1 E011)
Documentation of applicable AI laws and standards, required data protections, and compliance strategies (AIUC-1 E012)

NDS-06.name: AI Data Use & Consent Policies
NDS-06.expanded_definition: Formal policies governing how customer data is used for AI model training, inference processing, and output generation — covering input data rights, output ownership, data retention, opt-out mechanisms, and transparent communication to customers.
NDS-06.ai_rmf_mapping: Govern / Manage — data governance policies and customer rights.
maturity_criteria: Published AI input data policy covering how customer data is used for model training, inference processing, and data retention periods (AIUC-1 A001)
Published AI output data policy covering output ownership, usage rights, opt-out, and deletion rights (AIUC-1 A002)
Customer consent mechanisms for AI data processing with clear opt-in/opt-out controls
Data retention schedules specific to AI training data, inference logs, and generated outputs
Regular review and communication of data use policies to customers and stakeholders

NDS-07.name: Cross-Customer Data Isolation
NDS-07.expanded_definition: Multi-tenant data isolation controls preventing cross-customer data exposure when AI systems process or combine data from multiple customers — including model isolation, inference context separation, and training data segregation.
NDS-07.ai_rmf_mapping: Govern / Manage / Measure — tenant isolation governance and verification.
maturity_criteria: Safeguards preventing cross-customer data exposure when combining data from multiple sources (AIUC-1 A005)
Tenant-isolated model fine-tuning preventing data leakage between customer workloads
Inference context isolation ensuring one customer's data does not influence another's outputs
Training data segregation controls with verified isolation for multi-tenant model training
Regular testing and validation of cross-customer isolation boundaries

NDS-08.name: Intellectual Property & Copyright Safeguards
NDS-08.expanded_definition: Controls preventing AI systems from leaking organizational intellectual property and confidential information, and preventing AI outputs from violating copyrights, trademarks, or other third-party IP rights.
NDS-08.ai_rmf_mapping: Govern / Manage — IP governance and output content controls.
maturity_criteria: Safeguards preventing AI systems from leaking company intellectual property or confidential information (AIUC-1 A004)
Controls preventing AI outputs from violating copyrights, trademarks, or third-party intellectual property rights (AIUC-1 A007)
Content filtering mechanisms detecting potential IP-infringing output patterns
Training data provenance verification to identify and exclude copyrighted material where required
IP risk assessment process for new AI use cases and output types

DSO-01.name: Secure ML CI/CD
DSO-01.expanded_definition: Security-integrated ML CI/CD pipelines — including dependency scanning, model signing, reproducible build environments, and automated security gates before model artifacts are published.
DSO-01.ai_rmf_mapping: Manage / Measure / Govern — integrate trustworthy characteristics in SDLC and verify.
maturity_criteria: Dependency scanning (SCA) for all ML pipeline packages and libraries
Model signing with cryptographic verification before registry publication
Reproducible training environments (pinned dependencies, deterministic builds)
Static analysis and linting for ML pipeline code (notebooks, scripts, configs)
Automated security gates that block pipeline promotion on policy violations

DSO-02.name: Model & Dataset Lineage / Versioning
DSO-02.expanded_definition: Immutable versioning and lineage tracking for all models and datasets — enabling full traceability from training data through model artifacts to production deployments, with rollback capability.
DSO-02.ai_rmf_mapping: Map / Manage — lifecycle traceability and controlled change.
maturity_criteria: Immutable versioning for all model artifacts (weights, configs, code snapshots)
Dataset versioning with diff capability and change attribution
Lineage graph linking data sources → training runs → model versions → deployments
One-click rollback to any previous model version in production
Retention and archival policies for deprecated model/dataset versions

DSO-03.name: TEVV & Adversarial Testing Before Release
DSO-03.expanded_definition: Robust Testing, Evaluation, Verification, and Validation (TEVV) applied before any model or AI feature is released — including adversarial robustness testing, bias evaluation, safety checks, reliability testing, red-team exercises, and pre-deployment internal testing aligned with AIUC-1 mandates.
DSO-03.ai_rmf_mapping: Measure / Manage — testing and risk treatment.
maturity_criteria: Adversarial robustness testing against known attack vectors including prompt injection and jailbreak attempts aligned with adversarial threat taxonomy (AIUC-1 B001)
Bias and fairness evaluation across protected demographic groups
Safety and toxicity testing for generative AI outputs
Reliability and performance regression testing against baseline metrics
Red-team exercises simulating realistic adversarial scenarios
Internal pre-deployment testing across all risk categories for system changes requiring formal review or approval (AIUC-1 C002)

DSO-04.name: Risk-Gated Promotion to Production
DSO-04.expanded_definition: Controlled promotion of AI models to production through risk-based gates — including HITL approvals, staged rollouts (canary/blue-green), kill-switch mechanisms, automatic rollback triggers, and documented accountability for system change approvals.
DSO-04.ai_rmf_mapping: Govern / Manage — decision rights and operational controls.

E007.requirement: Document system change approvals (merged with E004)
E007.note: Merged with E004 in Q1 2026 update

maturity_criteria: HITL approval required before production deployment of high-risk models
Staged rollout (canary, blue-green, shadow) with traffic percentage controls
Kill-switch capability for immediate production model disablement
Automatic rollback triggers based on performance/safety metric thresholds
Deployment approval audit trail with approver identity and justification
Documented accountability for AI system changes requiring formal review, with assigned leads and approval evidence for each change (AIUC-1 E004)

DSO-05.name: Auditability & Lineage Graph
DSO-05.expanded_definition: Graph-based audit trail for production AI systems — linking source code, training data, model versions, configuration changes, inference decisions, and downstream outcomes into a queryable accountability structure for regulatory and forensic purposes.
DSO-05.ai_rmf_mapping: Map / Govern / Measure — lifecycle traceability, governance, and continuous assurance.
maturity_criteria: Graph structure linking: code commit → dataset version → training run → model artifact → deployment → inference decision → outcome
Queryable lineage for any production decision (trace back to training data and code)
Tamper-evident or immutable storage of graph nodes and edges
Timeline reconstruction capability for incident investigation and root-cause analysis
Integration with GRC/compliance platforms for automated evidence export

DSO-06.name: Independent Third-Party Testing Programs
DSO-06.expanded_definition: Mandated engagement of expert third parties to evaluate AI system robustness at minimum quarterly intervals — covering harmful output testing, out-of-scope output testing, customer-defined risk testing, hallucination testing, and tool call safety testing. Aligns with AIUC-1's testing-based assurance model.
DSO-06.ai_rmf_mapping: Measure / Govern — external assurance and continuous evaluation.
maturity_criteria: Expert third-party evaluation of system robustness to harmful outputs (distressed, angry, offensive, biased, deceptive) at least every 3 months (AIUC-1 C010)
Expert third-party evaluation of system robustness to out-of-scope outputs (political discussion, healthcare advice) at least every 3 months (AIUC-1 C011)
Expert third-party evaluation of system robustness to customer-defined high-risk outputs per risk taxonomy at least every 3 months (AIUC-1 C012)
Expert third-party evaluation of hallucinated outputs at least every 3 months (AIUC-1 D002)
Expert third-party evaluation of tool call safety (unauthorized actions, restricted information access, scope violations) at least every 3 months (AIUC-1 D004)

TRM-01.name: Model Governance & Acceptable Use
TRM-01.expanded_definition: Formal governance processes for AI models — covering approval workflows, ownership assignment, lifecycle state management, decommission procedures, and an organizational AI acceptable use policy defining permitted and prohibited AI behaviors.
TRM-01.ai_rmf_mapping: Govern — clear roles, policies, and oversight.

Established and implemented AI acceptable use policy defining permitted uses, prohibited behaviors, and breach consequences (AIUC-1 E010)

TRM-02.name: AI Risk Assessment & Taxonomy
TRM-02.expanded_definition: Structured risk assessment for each AI use case — evaluating impact, context, affected stakeholders, failure modes, and risk appetite. Extended with formal risk taxonomy covering harmful, out-of-scope, and hallucinated output categories with severity ratings.
TRM-02.ai_rmf_mapping: Map / Govern — context & impact mapping with policy alignment.

Impact classification (low/medium/high/critical) with defined criteria

Failure mode analysis with probability and severity estimation

AI risk taxonomy categorizing risks across harmful outputs, out-of-scope outputs, hallucinated outputs, tool call risks, and other application-specific risks with severity ratings (AIUC-1 C001)

TRM-03.name: Trustworthiness & Transparency Controls
TRM-03.expanded_definition: Technical and procedural controls ensuring AI trustworthiness across multiple dimensions — including fairness/bias mitigation, explainability/interpretability, privacy preservation, robustness/reliability guarantees, and system transparency through model cards, datasheets, and interpretability reports.
TRM-03.ai_rmf_mapping: Measure / Manage — trustworthy characteristics implementation & evaluation.

TRM-04.name: AI Incident Response, Failure Plans & Monitoring
TRM-04.expanded_definition: Operational monitoring and incident response capabilities purpose-built for AI-specific failure modes — including hallucinations, jailbreaks, data leakage, model drift, and adversarial exploitation. Extended with documented AI failure plans covering security breaches, harmful outputs, and hallucinations with assigned accountability and remediation procedures.
TRM-04.ai_rmf_mapping: Measure / Manage — continuous monitoring and incident handling.

E001.requirement: AI failure plan for security breaches

E002.requirement: AI failure plan for harmful outputs

maturity_criteria: AI-specific incident response runbooks covering hallucinations, jailbreaks, and data leakage
Real-time monitoring dashboards for model performance, drift, and safety metrics
Automated alerting on anomalous AI behavior with severity classification
Post-incident review process with root-cause analysis and control improvement
Integration with enterprise SOC workflows and escalation procedures
Documented AI failure plan for security and privacy breaches with accountable owners, notification procedures, and remediation with third-party support (legal, PR, insurers) (AIUC-1 E001)
Documented AI failure plan for harmful AI outputs causing significant customer harm with accountable owners and remediation procedures (AIUC-1 E002)
Documented AI failure plan for hallucinated AI outputs causing substantial customer financial loss with accountable owners and remediation procedures (AIUC-1 E003)

TRM-05.name: Lineage & Accountability Graph
TRM-05.expanded_definition: Governance-layer accountability graph that connects AI model decisions to organizational governance artifacts — linking risk assessments, approval records, policy versions, audit findings, and stakeholder impact analyses into a unified accountability structure. Complements the production lineage graph (DSO-05) by adding the governance and compliance dimension.
TRM-05.ai_rmf_mapping: Govern / Map / Measure — assurance, attestation, and continuous governance traceability.
maturity_criteria: Graph linking: risk assessment → approval record → policy version → model deployment → monitoring finding → remediation action
Accountability chain from any AI decision to the governance artifacts that authorized it
Artifact versioning so the policy/approval state at time-of-decision is reconstructable
Board/executive-level accountability dashboards derived from graph data
Cross-referencing with DSO-05 production lineage for end-to-end traceability

TRM-06.name: Enterprise & AIUC-1 Framework Crosswalk
TRM-06.expanded_definition: Maintained mapping from this framework's controls to enterprise and regulatory frameworks — including NIST CSF, ISO/IEC 42001, EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, AIUC-1, MITRE ATLAS, OWASP Top 10 for LLM, and sector-specific requirements — enabling unified compliance reporting.
TRM-06.ai_rmf_mapping: Govern — assurance & attestations through standards mapping.
maturity_criteria: Control-level crosswalk to NIST CSF 2.0 and NIST AI RMF
Mapping to ISO/IEC 42001 (AI Management System) requirements
EU AI Act risk-tier alignment with compliance gap analysis
AIUC-1 requirement-level crosswalk mapping each A001–F002 requirement to framework sub-pillars
Sector-specific regulatory mapping (healthcare, financial services, defense, etc.)
Crosswalk maintained as a living document with change tracking and review cadence

TRM-07.name: AI Quality Management System
TRM-07.expanded_definition: Establishes a quality management system for AI systems proportionate to organizational size — covering regular internal process reviews, documentation standards, approval workflows, and continuous improvement cycles for AI operations.
TRM-07.ai_rmf_mapping: Govern / Manage — process quality and internal oversight.
maturity_criteria: Quality management system for AI systems proportionate to organizational size and complexity (AIUC-1 E013)
Regular internal reviews of key AI processes with documented review records and approvals (AIUC-1 E008)
Defined quality metrics and KPIs for AI development, deployment, and operations
Continuous improvement cycle incorporating lessons learned from incidents, testing, and reviews
Documentation standards for AI system changes, processes, and approvals

TRM-08.name: Societal Risk & Misuse Prevention
TRM-08.expanded_definition: Controls and guardrails preventing AI systems from being used or exploited for societal harm — including AI-enabled cyber attacks, exploitation, and catastrophic misuse involving chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear (CBRN) threats.
TRM-08.ai_rmf_mapping: Govern / Manage — societal risk governance and safety controls.
maturity_criteria: Guardrails preventing AI-enabled misuse for cyber attacks and exploitation (AIUC-1 F001)
Guardrails preventing AI-enabled catastrophic misuse: chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear (CBRN) threats (AIUC-1 F002)
Dual-use risk assessment for AI capabilities with potential for misuse
Monitoring for adversarial attempts to repurpose AI systems for harmful activities
Incident reporting and coordination with law enforcement or national security agencies when misuse is detected

SAF-01.name: AI Risk Taxonomy & Output Classification
SAF-01.expanded_definition: Establishment and maintenance of a comprehensive AI risk taxonomy that categorizes risks within harmful, out-of-scope, and hallucinated outputs, tool calls, and other application-specific risks — with severity ratings and classification criteria informing all downstream safety controls.
SAF-01.ai_rmf_mapping: Govern / Map — risk categorization and context mapping.
maturity_criteria: AI risk taxonomy established covering harmful outputs, out-of-scope outputs, hallucinated outputs, and tool call risks with severity ratings (AIUC-1 C001)
Application-specific risk categories defined based on business context and user population
Severity rating system with clear escalation thresholds (info, warning, critical, emergency)
Taxonomy reviewed and updated at least quarterly to reflect emerging risk patterns
Taxonomy integrated into testing, monitoring, and incident response processes

SAF-02.name: Harmful Output Prevention
SAF-02.expanded_definition: Technical controls and safeguards preventing AI systems from generating harmful outputs — including distressed outputs, angry responses, high-risk advice, offensive content, bias, deception, and customer-defined high-risk outputs per the established risk taxonomy.
SAF-02.ai_rmf_mapping: Manage / Measure — output safety enforcement and evaluation.
maturity_criteria: Safeguards preventing harmful outputs including distressed outputs, angry responses, high-risk advice, offensive content, bias, and deception (AIUC-1 C003)
Safeguards preventing additional high-risk outputs as defined in the organization's AI risk taxonomy (AIUC-1 C005)
Multi-layer content safety filters (input validation, output scanning, post-generation review)
Contextual awareness controls adjusting safety thresholds based on use case and user population
Measurable harmful output rate tracking with defined reduction targets

SAF-03.name: Scope Boundary & Output Vulnerability Prevention
SAF-03.expanded_definition: Controls preventing AI systems from generating out-of-scope outputs (e.g., political discussion, healthcare advice beyond authorized scope) and preventing security vulnerabilities in outputs that could impact users — including code injection, data exfiltration, and other output-mediated attacks.
SAF-03.ai_rmf_mapping: Manage / Measure — scope governance and output security.
maturity_criteria: Safeguards preventing out-of-scope outputs such as political discussion, healthcare advice, or other topics outside the system's authorized domain (AIUC-1 C004)
Safeguards preventing security vulnerabilities in outputs from impacting users, including code injection and data exfiltration via output payloads (AIUC-1 C006)
Defined scope boundaries for each AI deployment with explicit permitted and prohibited topic lists
Output sanitization pipeline preventing injection attacks through AI-generated content
Scope violation tracking and reporting with drift analysis over time

SAF-04.name: Safety Monitoring, Flagging & Human Escalation
SAF-04.expanded_definition: Real-time monitoring of AI outputs across risk categories with automated flagging of high-risk outputs for human review, continuous monitoring dashboards, and mechanisms for user feedback and intervention — enabling rapid detection and response to safety violations.
SAF-04.ai_rmf_mapping: Measure / Manage — continuous safety monitoring and response.
maturity_criteria: Alerting system that flags high-risk outputs for human review with prioritized escalation queues (AIUC-1 C007)
Monitoring of AI systems across all defined risk categories with dashboards and trend analysis (AIUC-1 C008)
Mechanisms enabling real-time user feedback collection and intervention (pause, override, report) during AI interactions (AIUC-1 C009)
Safety incident response SLAs defining maximum time-to-review for flagged outputs by severity
Feedback loop from monitoring findings back to safety control tuning and risk taxonomy updates

SAF-05.name: Output Limitation & Information Leakage Prevention
SAF-05.expanded_definition: Controls limiting AI output fidelity and applying obfuscation techniques to safeguard against information leakage — preventing AI systems from exposing sensitive data, system internals, or other information that could be used for adversarial purposes through output manipulation.
maturity_criteria: Output limitation and obfuscation techniques safeguarding against information leakage through AI outputs (AIUC-1 B009)
Response filtering preventing exposure of system prompts, configurations, or internal data
Fidelity reduction controls for sensitive output categories (financial data, personal data, proprietary information)
Output length and detail controls preventing exhaustive data extraction through iterative querying
Testing and validation of output limitation controls against known extraction techniques

REL-01.name: Hallucination Prevention & Detection
REL-01.expanded_definition: Technical controls and safeguards preventing AI systems from generating hallucinated outputs — including factual grounding mechanisms, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), output verification chains, confidence scoring, and citation requirements.
REL-01.ai_rmf_mapping: Manage / Measure — reliability enforcement and evaluation.
maturity_criteria: Safeguards or technical controls preventing hallucinated outputs (AIUC-1 D001)
Factual grounding mechanisms (RAG, knowledge base verification, citation requirements)
Confidence scoring for AI outputs with low-confidence flagging or suppression
Hallucination detection in output pipeline (fact-checking, self-consistency checks)
Measurable hallucination rate tracking with defined thresholds and improvement targets

REL-02.name: Tool Call Safety & Scope Control
REL-02.expanded_definition: Controls ensuring AI agent tool calls remain within authorized scope — preventing execution of unauthorized actions, access to restricted information, and decisions beyond the agent's intended boundaries. Covers tool selection validation, parameter sanitization, and execution monitoring.
REL-02.ai_rmf_mapping: Manage / Measure — operational safety for agentic tool interactions.
maturity_criteria: Safeguards preventing tool calls from executing unauthorized actions, accessing restricted information, or making decisions beyond intended scope (AIUC-1 D003)
Tool allowlist with explicit definition of permitted tools and authorized parameters per agent context
Parameter validation and sanitization before tool execution
Real-time tool call monitoring with automatic blocking of out-of-scope requests
Tool call audit logging with full parameter capture and execution results

REL-03.name: Reliability Assurance Testing
REL-03.expanded_definition: Independent testing programs for AI reliability — covering hallucination evaluation and tool call safety testing performed by expert third parties at regular intervals to provide external assurance of output reliability.
REL-03.ai_rmf_mapping: Measure — external assurance of reliability characteristics.
maturity_criteria: Expert third-party evaluation of hallucinated outputs at least every 3 months (AIUC-1 D002)
Expert third-party evaluation of tool call safety at least every 3 months (AIUC-1 D004)
Defined reliability benchmarks and acceptance criteria for third-party test results
Remediation tracking for reliability issues identified through third-party testing
Trend analysis of reliability metrics across testing cycles

weeks_1_3.name: Stand Up Governance & AIUC-1 Gap Analysis
activities: Charter an AI Risk Council; define roles for model owners, product owners, security, privacy, legal
Publish acceptable-use policy for AI (data classes allowed/blocked, HITL requirements) (AIUC-1 E010)
Establish AI risk taxonomy covering harmful, out-of-scope, and hallucinated output categories (AIUC-1 C001)
Baseline current state: score all 40 sub-pillars at Level 1–5
Map AIUC-1 requirements to current controls and identify gaps
Document AI data use and consent policies (AIUC-1 A001, A002)

weeks_2_5.name: Inventory, Risk-Map & Data Privacy
activities: Create system of record for all AI models, agents, and vendor AI features
Complete context & impact mapping per AI RMF Map function
Tag genAI vs. predictive vs. agentic workloads for COSAiS alignment
Implement AI disclosure mechanisms (AIUC-1 E016)
Establish cross-customer data isolation controls (AIUC-1 A005)
Implement IP and copyright safeguards (AIUC-1 A004, A007)
Conduct vendor due diligence for foundation model providers (AIUC-1 E006)

weeks_4_8.name: Foundational Protections & Safety Controls
activities: Enforce least-privilege IAM on AI workspaces and endpoints (AIUC-1 B007)
Network-isolate training environments; apply WAF/rate-limit at inference endpoints (AIUC-1 B004)
Enable encryption at rest and in transit for all AI artifacts (AIUC-1 B008)
Implement TEVV gates with adversarial robustness testing (AIUC-1 B001, C002)
Deploy harmful output prevention safeguards (AIUC-1 C003, C005)
Deploy scope boundary enforcement (AIUC-1 C004, C006)
Implement hallucination prevention controls (AIUC-1 D001)
Implement tool call safety controls (AIUC-1 D003)
Deploy output limitation and obfuscation controls (AIUC-1 B009)
Implement PII leakage prevention safeguards (AIUC-1 A006)

weeks_6_12.name: Measure, Monitor, Third-Party Testing & Compliance
activities: Stand up model telemetry for drift, jailbreak attempts, and leakage
Deploy safety monitoring with human escalation (AIUC-1 C007, C008, C009)
Define AI failure plans for security breaches, harmful outputs, and hallucinations (AIUC-1 E001, E002, E003)
Deploy auditability & lineage graph (DSO-05) and accountability graph (TRM-05)
Establish quality management system (AIUC-1 E013, E008)
Implement societal risk guardrails (AIUC-1 F001, F002)
Engage expert third parties for quarterly testing program (AIUC-1 C010, C011, C012, D002, D004)
Prepare AIUC-1 compliance evidence packs and re-score all 40 sub-pillars
Document processing locations and regulatory compliance (AIUC-1 E011, E012)
